name: v2.15.0 - MINOR - Usenet fallback through SABnzbd, faster metadata and reads, and user-reported fixes
body:
# v2.15.0 (2026-09-20)

## New Features
- When DroppedNeedle can't fetch an NZB itself - an indexer only SABnzbd can reach - it now hands SABnzbd the URL instead of failing the download. Definitive indexer errors still fail fast. ([#457](https://github.com/DroppedNeedle/DroppedNeedle/pull/457)) (@daranto)

## Fixes
- Finamp can stream again: PlaybackInfo responses now carry every source field its parser requires, instead of crashing playback on a missing key. (#438)
- A transient stall mid-scan no longer fails the whole run. The scope is re-walked within the shared restart budget, and only a still-wedged walk fails. (#444)
- "Retry all failed" now retries only the newest failure per album or track instead of re-dispatching every historical failure.
- Library Management previews no longer show a stale banner while still planning, and when inputs do change the preview names the changed files (up to five) plus a count.
- Long planning runs no longer fail with a stale-input error just because unrelated catalog maintenance touched other albums: previews are now sealed against their own selected inputs. ([#475](https://github.com/DroppedNeedle/DroppedNeedle/pull/475)) (@alceasan)
- Files sitting in `.recycle` no longer resurface as separate albums: the default recycle bin directory is now excluded from scans. ([#471](https://github.com/DroppedNeedle/DroppedNeedle/pull/471)) (@andysom25)
- Holding a verified edition-conversion candidate for review no longer crashes; it is held as intended. ([#469](https://github.com/DroppedNeedle/DroppedNeedle/pull/469)) (@andysom25)
- Feishin works with transcoding disabled again: a max bitrate of 0 is treated as unset, per OpenSubsonic. ([#468](https://github.com/DroppedNeedle/DroppedNeedle/pull/468)) (@andysom25)
- AudioDB toggle labels in settings no longer overlap their descriptions. ([#472](https://github.com/DroppedNeedle/DroppedNeedle/pull/472)) (@andysom25)
- Newznab releases whose password status is unknown (negative values from aggregators) are no longer rejected as protected; only a positive flag blocks them. ([#456](https://github.com/DroppedNeedle/DroppedNeedle/pull/456)) (@daranto)
- The cache stats view loads again: the cache service is now built with its response store instead of raising a TypeError. ([#443](https://github.com/DroppedNeedle/DroppedNeedle/pull/443)) (@Barrykilby)

## Performance
- MusicBrainz lookups now pre-resolve merged-entity redirects from a persisted local map instead of re-issuing the same requests, and upstream rate limits now surface as proper 429 responses with Retry-After.
- Artist discography warming polls stop after about 60 seconds per mount instead of polling forever when the backend is stuck.
- Database reads reuse one SQLite connection per thread instead of re-parsing the schema on every operation. ([#470](https://github.com/DroppedNeedle/DroppedNeedle/pull/470)) (@funkypenguin)

## Docs & Chores
- Routine dependency bumps across the frontend and backend, including FastAPI 0.118.3 to 0.141.1 (route-allowlist tests now read the flattened OpenAPI surface) and eslint 9 to 10.

name: v2.14.1 - PATCH - stale dry-run recovery, live retry progress, and one event stream per tab
body:
# v2.14.1 (2026-09-14)

## Fixes
- The Library Management automation tab now flags roots whose dry-run activation has gone stale, and offers a fresh dry run to bring them back. Roots where a dry run can't help are marked paused instead of stale.
- Upgrading no longer pauses the organizer when the only thing that changed is a project default you never touched. Activations that reviewed the old defaults now carry forward instead of demanding a fresh dry run.
- Retrying a held download now shows live progress - stage and file counts - as the organizer works through it, and starting a second retry while one is already running is refused instead of doubling up.
- Live updates (following, now playing, sync status, library activity) now share one stream per browser tab instead of four separate connections, and each user gets their own request budget so one busy user can't crowd out the others.

name: v2.14.0 - MINOR - Best-fit editions from your files' tags, per-track removal, and user-reported fixes
body:
# v2.14.0 (2026-09-13)

## New Features
- When every embedded release tag in an album's files names the same pressing, album pages now show it as the best-fit edition, with a note saying where the pick came from.
- Uncertain editions moved into their own confirm lane in review. Confirming one only picks which pressing is shown, and your files never change there.
- Albums where only some tracks carry embedded release tags now identify against the agreed release instead of stalling, as long as the untagged rest doesn't contradict it.

## Fixes
- Settled album identities stay settled: a re-scan that comes back with weaker evidence no longer files them back into review.
- Collaboration albums with full track proof now pass the artist check instead of landing in review.
- Undoing an automatic edition now clears cached views, so the restored identity shows up everywhere instead of lingering stale.
- Edition pins and stored identities now match case-insensitively.
- A download that finds its destination already occupied by a file the catalog can't attribute is now held for review instead of being reported a success. (#418)
- Organizing an album now carries back covers, booklets, and disc artwork along with it by default, so leftover artwork stops stranding the old folder behind. (#401)
- An edition conversion left stranded by a discarded preview can now be applied, cancelled, or re-previewed instead of sitting stuck. (#425)
- Subsonic clients now see the transcoding extension advertised, matching what the server already supports. (#431)
- Matched albums grew a per-track Remove file action, so one track's file can go without touching the rest. ([#417](https://github.com/DroppedNeedle/DroppedNeedle/pull/417)) (@andysom25)
- Stopping a watch while scouting is still running no longer lets the download start afterwards. ([#420](https://github.com/DroppedNeedle/DroppedNeedle/pull/420)) (@SomeVlad)
- Album tracklists now always resolve against the authoritative release, so a partial album can't read as complete and stall Wanted early, and stale aliases that hid the real owner are repaired. ([#419](https://github.com/DroppedNeedle/DroppedNeedle/pull/419)) (@SomeVlad)
- Library Management no longer lets catalog rows whose files are gone reserve destinations and block a surviving edition. ([#416](https://github.com/DroppedNeedle/DroppedNeedle/pull/416)) (@alceasan)
- Merged MusicBrainz entities now resolve through BrainzMash redirects instead of failing permanently. ([#426](https://github.com/DroppedNeedle/DroppedNeedle/pull/426)) (@780Farva)
- Edition conversion previews now pin the live file revisions, so kept previews stop reading as changed and refusing to apply. ([#427](https://github.com/DroppedNeedle/DroppedNeedle/pull/427)) (@780Farva)
- Applying an edition conversion to a source album with no track identities no longer crashes. ([#428](https://github.com/DroppedNeedle/DroppedNeedle/pull/428)) (@780Farva)

## Performance
- Home and Discover cache warming triggered by demand now yields to interactive traffic instead of competing with it. ([#429](https://github.com/DroppedNeedle/DroppedNeedle/pull/429)) (@andysom25)

## Docs & Chores
- Routine dependency bumps across the frontend and backend, plus icon and test-helper migrations for the new lucide-svelte.

name: v2.12.0 - MINOR - Navidrome playlist export, per-album edition pins, and user-reported fixes
body:
# v2.12.0 (2026-09-05)

## New Features
- DroppedNeedle can now export playlists as .m3u8 files into a folder Navidrome scans, so playlists show up in Navidrome. It is off by default. Turn it on under the Navidrome settings, pick the export folder and whether private playlists are included, and exports refresh on a schedule or with Sync Now. Exported files carry an ownership marker, so a playlist file you made by hand is never overwritten or deleted even if a name collides. ([#379](https://github.com/DroppedNeedle/DroppedNeedle/pull/379)) (@fluxopex)
- Starting the server without the migration launcher now logs a warning at boot saying catalog migrations did not run and telling you to restore the image CMD, instead of skipping them silently.

## Fixes
- Edition pins now work per album instead of per release group, and when several albums share a group a picker dialog asks which one you mean. Deleted albums no longer leave ghosts behind that block pinning, and albums with no owned files stay on the group page instead of dropping off it. (#382)
- Library catalog repairs now queue one job per album while one is already running, so slow metadata responses no longer flood the task list with dozens of maintenance jobs. (#386)
- Spotify album requests that resolve through an ISRC now prefer the requested artist's release instead of landing on a Various Artists compilation that happens to contain the track, which used to fail the tag check after download. (#385)
- Organization previews no longer crash on albums without an exact release MBID. The Cover Art Archive lookup is skipped when there is no MBID to query. (#384)
- Spotify-imported playlist tracks with no playable source now heal themselves once you acquire the missing album, picking the best available source instead of sitting unplayable. (#381)
- Organization previews now say in plain words why each file is blocked or waiting, and show when optional enrichment was deferred and for which source.
- If you close the browser mid-review, reopening the preview re-issues your apply token instead of orphaning the planned work.
- First-run migration skips files the catalog already owns instead of re-staging them, and a failed upgrade now records a safe summary of what went wrong plus the full error in the logs.
- Spotify imports now read a playlist's track count from its items, falling back to the tracks summary when items are absent.
- The player retries a failed track once and tries an alternate source before giving up and skipping ahead.
- Playlist sources backed by a media server you never configured now fail fast with a clear error naming the missing setup, instead of failing obscurely halfway through.
- Jellyfin playlist imports no longer store an unresolvable album GUID as a track's album link, so album links in imported playlists point at real albums.
- The Last.fm and ListenBrainz settings links now point at the profile scrobbling settings, where the options they describe actually live.
- Small screens get an overflow menu holding the destinations that do not fit the bar, so every page stays reachable on a phone.
- The Library item in the nav bar only lights up on Library pages now, instead of staying active elsewhere.

name: v2.11.1 - PATCH - retirement banner removed

- The retirement banner is gone, along with its boot-log warning. v2.11.0 delivered that notice to the old `habirabbu/*` images, and keeping it would only nag installs that already switched.

name: v2.11.0 - MINOR - legacy image retirement notice, Finamp login fix, and Plex and library fixes
body:
# v2.11.0 (2026-09-04)

## New Features
- If you still pull an old `habirabbu/*` image, v2.11 shows a banner telling you to switch your compose file to `droppedneedle/droppedneedle` (or `ghcr.io/droppedneedle/droppedneedle`), then pull and restart. Old names stop receiving updates after v2.11.x. Already switched means nothing changes, and your library and settings are untouched.

## Fixes
- Plex linking no longer tells you that you lack server access when plex.tv returns a response it cannot use. It now reports that access could not be verified, and it keeps the tokens from that response out of the logs.
- Finamp can log in again. The Jellyfin login reply now includes the Policy fields Finamp requires, instead of crashing on a missing value.
- The Library All Tracks page requests covers with the provider release-group id, so identified tracks show artwork instead of missing it.
- Saving the download policy after adding or removing a quality recipe now updates the preference order to match the new range instead of saving the stale one.

## Docs & Chores
- README rewritten for the DroppedNeedle org move, CLA and its workflow removed. A spec file using the reserved `+page` name was renamed so it no longer blocks builds.

name: v2.10.2 - PATCH - download imports rejoin their album, requests resolve real names, SABnzbd shows live status
body:
# v2.10.2 (2026-09-04)

## Fixes

- Download imports after an edition switch no longer create a duplicate album. Imports rejoin the album that already owns the release group instead of minting a new one, which also ends the 409 Conflict when fetching missing tracks that way (part of #301).
- Ghost editions whose files are already gone can now be removed. Deleting one cleans up the leftover catalog rows instead of failing.
- Album requests with a missing or placeholder name now resolve the real artist and title from MusicBrainz instead of searching for "Unknown". Batch requests skip items that still cannot be resolved instead of recording them broken.
- Name resolution only returns a 400 when the release is genuinely unknown or MusicBrainz cannot be reached. Unexpected errors now surface as themselves instead of being masked as a bad request.
- The SABnzbd settings card shows the live connection status from your saved settings as soon as you open it. No need to run Test just to see whether it is connected.

name: v2.10.1 - PATCH - tougher Soulseek matching and recovery, plus review, home, and fresh-install fixes
body:
# v2.10.1 (2026-09-03)

## Fixes

- Soulseek searches now query the primary artist only. A multi-artist credit used to AND every name into the query so albums the network holds returned nothing, and album searches gain edition-stripped fallback rungs so "Euphoria (International Edition)" also tries plain "Euphoria" (part of #373).
- Errored Soulseek transfers can now recover from slskd's incomplete-downloads folder. A new optional setting under Download Client points at that folder, and per-file failover treats leftover partial bytes as a retry signal instead of a miss (#292).
- Pasted slskd API keys with stray whitespace now work, and a wrong key fails fast with a clear auth error instead of retrying. Test-connection also runs on its own breaker now, so a bad key check never poisons live download traffic (#193).
- Files whose names use a different Unicode spelling on the peer than on disk now resolve when exactly one matching file exists, instead of missing. Size mismatches are still rejected, but by the verifier, so the log says what actually went wrong.
- The home "Your Music" card now says how many albums need review and takes you straight to the review queue when something awaits a decision.
- The edition-finder search row wraps instead of overflowing in narrow dialogs.
- Fresh installs no longer fail library verification. An empty volume now initializes its database in place instead of going through stage-and-publish, and the post-rename settle check verifies the open handle before trusting the path view.

name: v2.10.0 - MINOR - an edition-confirm step for review, tougher downloads and upgrades, and user-reported fixes
body:
# v2.10.0 (2026-09-03)

This cycle covers 25 commits since v2.9.0. Library review gains an edition-confirm step for albums where the release is right but the exact edition is uncertain, downloads get harder to corrupt or stall, and three user-reported issues are fixed. Your library, settings, and database carry over, and standard installs need no action. Thanks to everyone for the reports.

## New Features

- Uncertain editions get their own review lane. When identification is confident about the release but not the exact pressing, the album now waits in an edition-confirm state with the ranked editions shown, instead of landing in generic review or picking the wrong edition on its own.

## Fixes

- Throttled provider responses no longer push albums into manual review. A transient gap during identification defers the album instead of asking you to resolve what is really a rate limit, and the run skips its extra lookup while throttled.
- Scan progress stays visible while identification catches up. The activity list now shows a drain row with what is still awaiting identification instead of going quiet after the file walk finishes.
- Soulseek downloads filed as `NN. Title` inside an album folder now match peers advertising the flat `Artist - Album - NN - Title` name, so those tracks stop missing and re-queuing.
- Truncated downloads are rejected by size before the tag read. A short file used to import as if whole because MP3 duration reads the header, not the audio; the completed folder is now preserved on local faults instead of cleaned up.
- Downloads import from disk when the transfer records read empty but every file sits complete in the completed folder (covers #131). No more re-downloading files you already have.
- A dead enqueue fails over to another peer instead of dying before the manifest exists (covers #285).
- Import failures log their real cause to the server log in sanitized form, and copystat errors no longer fail an otherwise good import (part of #185).
- The automatic upgrader's final promotion survives flaky Docker renames and fresh installs, with the live database verified before and after the swap.
- Legacy favorites, history, and compat references that point at nothing are skipped with redacted logging instead of failing the migration, and resumed runs count already-migrated rows instead of tripping validation.
- Genre enrichment no longer kills a whole management run when a breaker is open. The unreachable source is deferred and the run continues (fixes #370).
- Fixed the "No such column: te_provider_artist_id" crash by resolving catalog artists through credited artist identities (fixes #369).
- Linked Navidrome track and album counts no longer grow on every refresh. The service was extending the repository's cached list in place (fixes #371).
- Restored a missing Spotify callback path constant and a missing artwork-merge import, both one-line crash fixes.
- The local turntable deck shows the right cover when the stored URL is not remote, and the tonearm parks where it should.

## Security

- Cryptography floor raised to 50.0.1 for a CVE fix (from PR #356 by @app/dependabot).

## Docs & Chores

- The rest is dependency bumps (ruff, pytest-asyncio with pytest 8.4.2, mutagen, type stubs, vitest with a v4 config migration, a 20-package frontend group, adapter-auto, prettier-plugin-svelte, globals, from PRs #355 and #357-364 by @app/dependabot) plus tests, with no user-visible change.

## API notes (for scripts)

- Review items gain `edition_uncertain` and `ranked_edition_keys`, the review list accepts the `edition_to_confirm` state and returns `counts_by_reason_filtered`. Scan activity can carry a synthetic `identification-drain` work item, which is not a scan-run id so don't query it as one. Nothing else changed.

name: v2.9.0 - MINOR - quality recipes for downloads, re-checks for held tracks, and a round of Usenet and search fixes
body:
# v2.9.0 (2026-09-03)

This cycle covers 17 commits since v2.8.0. Download quality settings become named FLAC and MP3 recipes, and fingerprint-held tracks get a re-check button so one bad verdict no longer means downloading everything again. The rest is mostly Usenet and search fixes from user-reported issues. Your library, settings, and database carry over, and standard installs need no action. Thanks to @fluxopex for the Usenet completeness fix.

## New Features

- Download quality is now a set of named recipes. Settings > Download Policy offers FLAC recipes (CD, 24-bit tiers, hi-res) and MP3 recipes (bitrate tiers) in place of the old quality-order editor, and choices are checked on save so a bad combination is rejected up front instead of matching nothing.
- Held tracks can be re-checked. Holds now weigh file length as well as the recording match, each held card shows the expected track length, and a re-check button (single or bulk) re-runs the check on files already on disk. Confirmed tracks import normally; the rest stay held.

## Fixes

- Usenet imports no longer fail with "files=0" when the files land a moment later (fixes #245): completed tasks can be reimported, path remapping is stricter, unplaceable files stay visible, and delivery counts fall back to the asked tracklist when the manifest names no files (from PR #350 by @fluxopex).
- Cancelling an album's downloads stops its wanted watch too, and the Soulseek picker avoids peer folders that already came up empty. Two steps toward #255, which stays open.
- Search tolerates messy titles now. Newznab retries with punctuation stripped (fixes #259), and album matching folds apostrophes and paren-obfuscated tags like "O(verly) D(edicated)" that used to quarantine good files into a re-download loop (fixes #307).
- Album identification no longer crashes with "cannot unpack non-iterable coroutine" (fixes #349).
- The Official MusicBrainz card sticks when selected, including on installs with stale bindings.
- ListenBrainz backs off exponentially on rate limits even with no retry header from the server.
- Provider artist discovery is scoped per user, so accounts on shared installs stop seeing each other's results.
- The automatic upgrader retries through transient Docker bind-mount flaps instead of failing.
- The settings page has its two scrollbars back.

The remaining commits are tests and a versioned User-Agent for BrainzMash, with no user-visible change.

## API notes (for scripts)

- New `POST /downloads/held/reverify` (bulk, capped) and `POST /downloads/held/{held_id}/reverify` (single); held objects gain `expected_duration_seconds`. The download-policy settings moved from a quality-order list to named recipes. Nothing else changed.

name: v2.6.1 - PATCH - MusicBrainz requests work again after an upstream User-Agent block

# v2.6.1 (2026-08-24)

## Fixes

- MusicBrainz requests work again after its edge began dropping connections that used DroppedNeedle's old User-Agent. DroppedNeedle now sends a compliant app name, release version, short installation ID, maintainer contact, and project URL, with the project contact address used when an installation leaves that setting blank. Cover-art and background image requests no longer use the blocked prefix either.

name: v2.6.0 - MINOR - Library management suggests exact editions, local cover art comes first, and scans stop hanging
body:
# v2.6.0 (2026-08-17)

## Breaking Changes
_None._

## New Features

- Identity preparation now suggests an exact edition from stored identification evidence when an album has no accepted release, and adds a bulk "Accept editions" action to apply them all at once. Suggestions come from evidence gathered during past identification runs; ties break to the earliest Official edition, worldwide first. You can still override the choice from the album page afterwards.

## Fixes

- Cover art: folder images and art embedded in the audio files are now served before any online source, with a new "Prefer Local Cover Art" setting, on by default. Local covers keep working when an image provider is down.
- Cover images that stall on a direct CDN link now fall back to the covers proxy instead of hanging.
- Artist pages fetch the full discography in one pass with dedupe and caching. Long catalogs no longer show a partial slice, and repeat visits load faster.
- Library scans are bounded against hangs and outages, and each scan run now lists the paths that failed. A new master switch pauses all scan, identification, and organize work for the local library.
- Albums stuck churning through partial identification can now be left unmanaged: their valid release-group and recording links stay, and the management warnings stop.
- Background discovery precache and cover fetches back off while upstream services are down, so the app stays responsive and catches up on its own.
- The quality range slider in Settings no longer sticks when the two handles cross.
- The in-place auto-upgrade survives filesystems that don't honor atomic renames, like Docker Desktop for Windows bind mounts. It detects the failure and falls back to a verified direct copy; named volumes are still the recommended setup on Windows.

name: v2.5.0 - MINOR - Library Management gets an overview dashboard, clearer tabs, and plainer words
body:
# v2.5.0 (2026-08-16)

The Library Management page has been rebuilt around a new Overview dashboard: current work up top, library stats and quick actions below. Scanning, Organize files, and Automation sit behind a segmented tab control. The Scanning tab now has one primary "Scan for changes" action, the identity recheck panel moved next to the rest of the identity work, and the management pages say what things do in plainer words - "Library control room" and "Existing-match check" are gone.

name: v2.4.3 - PATCH - MusicBrainz outages no longer spin the library maintenance loop or flood the logs
body:
# v2.4.3 (2026-08-15)

## Fixes

- The "Maintaining the library catalog" job that could sit at "queued" for hours, burning CPU and filling the log, now waits quietly while MusicBrainz is down and picks up where it left off on its own once MusicBrainz responds again.

- A few releases carry MusicBrainz data in an unexpected shape, like a release group with no type or a release with no status. Those albums now decode fine, and from now on one odd release can't take MusicBrainz down for the rest of the library - search, downloads, and identification keep working.

- While MusicBrainz is rate-limiting or down, album identification waits politely instead of hammering failed requests. Libraries that identify from their own embedded tags keep processing through an outage.

- The log flood is gone. The "circuit breaker open" warning now appears at most every thirty seconds instead of several times a second, and expected failures no longer write an error line per call.

name: v2.4.2 - PATCH - Saved paths outside the library roots no longer block the upgrade, and anything left waiting imports when the roots return
body:
# v2.4.2 (2026-08-15)

## Fixes

- Library records whose paths fall outside the configured roots no longer stop the library upgrade. The upgrade completes and keeps those records waiting instead of failing. If an earlier image refused to start after a failed upgrade, this one retries on startup and finishes.

- If your music moved since it was last seen (a changed mount point, for example), the upgrade now looks for it before giving up. When the saved files check out at one location it points the root there or remaps the paths to the configured root, and anything it can't prove is left waiting rather than guessed at.

- Records left waiting are imported automatically later. Re-add the matching root on the Library settings page and the import runs on save; the app also checks once at every startup.

name: v2.4.1 - PATCH - Unmatched play history no longer blocks the library upgrade, and removed library roots can be restored
body:
# v2.4.1 (2026-08-15)

## Fixes

- Play history that the library upgrade can't match to a track no longer stops the upgrade. The entries are kept as-is instead, and when the same recording appears on several releases the upgrade narrows it down by album and track name instead of giving up.

- When an upgrade does fail, the error now says what went wrong. It names the failure reason, points at the detail file, and explains the options: switch back to your previous image, install a corrected one, or fix the data and restart.

- The library settings page no longer lets you remove every library root while the catalog still has tracks. DroppedNeedle refuses the save and suggests excluding the root's policy instead.

- Roots that disappeared from the configuration can be restored from the Library settings page. Their original identities and paths are recovered from the catalog, so a restore doesn't rescan everything as new.

name: v2.3.0 - MINOR - Free Music, import your purchases, where-to-buy links, and an experimental plugin API
body:
# v2.3.0 (2026-07-11)

## Breaking Changes
_None._

## New Features
- **Free Music.** A lawful source that ships with the app. It downloads Creative Commons and public-domain releases from the Internet Archive, with the licence shown before anything downloads. No account or API key, on by default, one toggle in Settings turns it off. Requests now work out of the box even with no download client configured.
- **Import your purchases.** Drop a zip or loose files onto your home page or the Downloads Import tab. They're identified by the scanner's pipeline (MusicBrainz tags, then AcoustID), tagged, organised into your library, and any matching request is resolved. A better-quality copy upgrades in place; anything unidentified waits under "Needs a match". Admin and trusted users can import.
- **Where to buy.** Album and artist pages now list where to buy, from MusicBrainz purchase links with iTunes and Bandcamp fallbacks. Stores are ordered by how fairly they pay artists, Bandcamp first. Optional affiliate tags (Amazon, Apple, Qobuz) earn the project a small commission at no cost to you, with a disclosure line and a Settings toggle to turn it off.
- **An experimental plugin API.** Third parties can add scrobblers and purchase-link providers, installed from a GitHub URL or the plugins folder. Plugins run in-process with no sandbox, so read the code before enabling. No plugin can download music. Full reference in PLUGINS.md.

## Fixes
- The YouTube player now stays inside Google's embed policies: a fixed 200x200 pop-out, visible while it plays, no background playback.

## Security
- The no-bundled-sources and no-P2P-protocol promises are now enforced in CI, and the audio-source plugin capability was removed so plugins can't be an acquisition source.
- OIDC PKCE is now an independent implementation, and a contributor licence agreement was added for pull requests.

## Docs & Chores
- Repo URLs and Docker images now point at the DroppedNeedle organisation, with legacy habirabbu tags kept on stable releases so older installs still update.

name: v2.2.0 - MINOR - Bring your Lidarr artists across, app-passwords on your Profile, and a quality policy that applies right away
body:
# v2.2.0 (2026-07-09)

## Breaking Changes
_None._

## New Features
- **Import your monitored artists from Lidarr.** Point DroppedNeedle at an existing Lidarr under Settings -> Lidarr Import, and every artist Lidarr monitors can become a follow here. Artists are matched on MusicBrainz ID, so nothing is guessed from a name. Any artist Lidarr already grabs new releases for comes across asking for the same treatment, and those requests are gathered into one approval batch that an admin accepts or rejects in a single click rather than artist by artist. Nothing is written back to Lidarr, and running the import again won't re-arm or alter artists you already follow.
- **App-passwords now live on your Profile.** Connecting Symfonium, Finamp, Feishin or any other Subsonic or Jellyfin client used to mean digging through a Settings page mostly full of toggles only an admin could touch. Every user now creates and revokes their own app-passwords from their own Profile page. Settings -> Connect Apps is now the admin's view: the server-side API toggles, plus a roster of every active app-password on the instance and who owns it, each one revocable in a click. As before, the password itself is shown once, at creation.

## Fixes
- Saving a quality policy takes effect straight away. Downloads used to keep enforcing whatever policy was loaded when the app started, so widening the range (allowing MP3 alongside FLAC, say) did nothing until you restarted DroppedNeedle.
- When a download is retried automatically, its stored candidate gets re-checked against the current quality range before it goes back out. A file picked under an older policy no longer slips through under the new one.
- The first-admin setup screen tells you what actually went wrong, whether that's a breached password or a bad username or email, instead of answering "Invalid setup data" to everything.

## Performance
- Searches stay responsive while a library scan is running. The scan's MusicBrainz lookups now queue behind whatever you're waiting on instead of competing with it.
- Fingerprinting scales with the host: fpcalc ran two at a time, and now runs one per core, up to four.

## Docs & Chores
- Layout fixes on the Connect Apps settings form.

name: v2.1.0 - MINOR - One-click fix for mistyped Newznab URLs, plus an Unraid template
body:
# v2.1.0 (2026-07-07)

## New Features
- **Newznab setup catches the /api mistake for you.** Paste a site's homepage into an indexer and hit Test, and DroppedNeedle now checks whether the real API is at `<url>/api`, which is where nzbgeek, ninjacentral, DrunkenSlug and the *arr apps all put it. When that responds, the test result shows a "Use .../api" button that fixes the URL in one click.

## Docs & Chores
- Added the official Unraid template and Community Applications profile, plus a new `SLSKD_DOWNLOADS_PATH` variable so Soulseek imports match your download mount out of the box.
- Tidied the example `docker-compose.yml` so it's shorter and easier to adapt.
- Clarified the README license: still AGPL-3.0, with commercial licensing available from the copyright holder.

name: v2.0.0 - MAJOR - Musicseerr is now DroppedNeedle: Lidarr removed, native library + multi-source downloads, and a whole lot more...
body:
# v2.0.0 (2026-07-07)

Musicseerr is now **DroppedNeedle**, and Lidarr is gone. Everything Lidarr used to do runs natively now: the app scans your library, reads and writes tags, fingerprints tracks, and organises files itself. Downloading is native too. Point it at your own Soulseek (slskd) and/or Usenet (SABnzbd, with built-in Newznab indexers) and it searches, downloads, verifies, and imports, per album or per track. It can also act as a Subsonic- and Jellyfin-compatible server, so your existing player apps stream straight from the library.

Your data carries over. Point the new image at the same config volume and your settings, database, and library are all still there.

## Moving from Musicseerr

- No more Lidarr. Set up slskd and/or SABnzbd under Settings -> Download Client instead.
- Everyone signs in once after upgrading (the session keys were renamed), and player state resets. Nothing else changes.
- Pulling `habirabbu/musicseerr:latest` moves you onto DroppedNeedle automatically. You can switch to `habirabbu/droppedneedle` whenever you like; both get the same builds.

## Highlights

- Native library engine: scanning, tag read/write, audio fingerprinting, and file organising, all in the app. A folder-consensus scanner identifies albums from the files on disk and holds uncertain imports for review with an audio preview.
- Multi-source downloads over Soulseek (slskd) and Usenet (SABnzbd with native Newznab indexers, no Prowlarr), per album or per track.
- Safer imports: auto-accept needs artist evidence, mismatched or wrong-length files are held for review, and an album only counts as complete once its tracklist is covered.
- Quality cutoff with automatic upgrades for admin and trusted users (better files replace worse ones, with a recycle bin), plus a global storage cap and per-user request and storage quotas for shared instances.
- A Wanted watcher that re-searches failed or incomplete requests over time and downloads verified finds on its own, with a Wanted tab to manage it.
- Home and Discover rebuilt into toggleable sections (queue deck, Top Picks, Listening Lounge, Deezer/iTunes previews, downloadable discovery batches), warmed in the background so pages open ready. A header health indicator flags when a source like MusicBrainz or Last.fm is struggling.
- New Releases as a release log with a 30 / 90 / 365-day selector, a hide-owned toggle, and in-library ticks, plus a sidebar badge for unseen releases.
- Upcoming events: DroppedNeedle watches Ticketmaster and Skiddle for concerts by artists you follow, filtered to your city.
- Playlist import from your connected sources with live Spotify refresh ([#108](https://github.com/HabiRabbu/DroppedNeedle/pull/108), @jma1ice), and a per-user Weekly Mix built from your listen history ([#110](https://github.com/HabiRabbu/DroppedNeedle/pull/110), @jma1ice).
- Manual reimport of downloads that failed inside slskd ([#105](https://github.com/HabiRabbu/DroppedNeedle/pull/105), @jma1ice), and a Wrapped integration for external newsletters ([#112](https://github.com/HabiRabbu/DroppedNeedle/pull/112), @jma1ice).
- Faster cold cover grids and navigation, live now-playing presence over SSE, and a long list of download-reliability and tagging fixes.

---

Thanks to everyone who ran the betas and reported the rough edges. This was a big rebuild.

name: v1.4.2 - PATCH - Fix playlist caching of empty results
body:
# v1.4.2 (2026-06-14)

## Fixes

- **Empty playlists no longer get cached forever.** If a library had no playlists on the first fetch, the empty result was cached and playlists would never appear even after creating new ones. The backend now skips caching when the result is empty, so playlists always show up when they exist (@HabiRabbu)

name: v1.4.1 - PATCH - Library Playlist banner fix + Scroll-reveal sections fix
body:
# v1.4.1 (2026-06-14)

## Fixes

- **Source playlists no longer cause the import banner to vanish.** Playlist data is now loaded outside the hub so the UI stays stable when browsing playlists across Jellyfin, Navidrome, and Plex (@HabiRabbu)
- **Tall scroll-reveal sections no longer leave blank gaps.** The reveal animation handles variable-height content properly, so long lists and playlists render without empty whitespace (@HabiRabbu)

name: v1.4.0 - MINOR - Multi-user auth arrives, PWA foundation, performance improvments, various fixes
body:
# v1.4.0 (2026-06-14)

## Breaking Changes
_None._

## New Features
- [#62](https://github.com/HabiRabbu/Musicseerr/pull/62), [#90](https://github.com/HabiRabbu/Musicseerr/pull/90) - **Multi-user authentication is here.** This has been one of the most long-awaited features in MusicSeerr since its release... and it's finally here. Local login, registration, and session management are all in, along with Plex, Jellyfin, and OIDC login flows. A public allowlist keeps things flexible for who can sign up. Huge thanks to @jma1ice for building the entire auth backend. It's an amazing piece of work that so many of you asked for.

- [#85](https://github.com/HabiRabbu/Musicseerr/pull/85) - The app now has the very first foundations to allow it to work like a real phone app. There's a bottom tab bar, proper iOS standalone metadata for Add to Home Screen, safe-area padding, and the player respects mobile spacing (@OmarB97)
- [#88](https://github.com/HabiRabbu/Musicseerr/pull/88) - OIDC login now supports PKCE (S256). Public clients that don't have a secret work out of the box, and everything follows OAuth 2.1 best practices (@gossip31)

## Fixes
- [#71](https://github.com/HabiRabbu/Musicseerr/pull/71) - The logo and nav padding now shrink down nicely on small screens so nothing overflows on mobile (fixes #70) (@halsandr)
- [#84](https://github.com/HabiRabbu/Musicseerr/pull/84) - Tapping a Navidrome track no longer leaves the player stuck at 0:00. Playback kicks off straight away instead of silently waiting for a `canplay` event that might never show up (@OmarB97)
- [#91](https://github.com/HabiRabbu/Musicseerr/pull/91) - Duplicate entries are gone from library results (fixes #80) (@HabiRabbu)
- [#92](https://github.com/HabiRabbu/Musicseerr/pull/92) - Large playlists load faster now because album sources resolve concurrently instead of one at a time (@HabiRabbu)

## Performance
- [#83](https://github.com/HabiRabbu/Musicseerr/pull/83) - Full-library Lidarr scans now cache for an hour instead of 5 minutes. Browsing a big library no longer kicks off expensive scans over and over (@OmarB97)
- [#93](https://github.com/HabiRabbu/Musicseerr/pull/93) - The backend uses less memory over time thanks to capped glibc arenas, periodic malloc_trim, and LRU-bounded now-playing tracking. The server stays lean during long listening sessions (@HabiRabbu)

## Security
- [#88](https://github.com/HabiRabbu/Musicseerr/pull/88) - OIDC login now uses PKCE (S256), following OAuth 2.1 recommendations for all client types (@gossip31)

## Docs & Chores
- [#67](https://github.com/HabiRabbu/Musicseerr/pull/67) - Fixed the broken Tubifarry link in the README (fixes #64) (@millionjt)

---

Some new infra experimentation is going on behind the scenes also to make things a bit more organised, which is always nice.
